IV. 
Support For IT Projects 
2 
Q. 
The SITP asserts (at 34) that based on a sample of projects, the 
3 
Company did not provide cost benefit analyses for many of the 
4 
projects reflected in its forecast of capital expenditures.  Do you 
5 
agree?    
6 
A. 
No, in the Company’s responses to IRs DPS-392 – 414, which are set 
7 
forth in Exhibit __ (SITP-1) at pages 2-2,790, the Company provided an 
8 
Investment Request Summary (“IRS”) or sanction paper for every project 
9 
included the Core IT Plan and each of the IT Transformation teams 
10 
provided support including business cases for each of the programs.  For 
11 
the Core IT programs, IRS and sanction papers have been the primary cost 
12 
benefit support provided to Staff for almost ten years.  These documents 
13 
provide cost and benefit information in a summarized and standard format 
14 
that allows for easy review of the scope of work being undertaken, the 
15 
benefits to be achieved, and the forecast costs broken down by CAPEX, 
16 
OPEX, and RTB.  In addition to the documentary support, the Company 
17 
held technical meetings with Staff to provide a more in-depth review of 
18 
the merits of each of the IT-related projects.  The Company believes that 
19 
there was adequate support in the documents and other information 
20 
provided to perform a project by project review.   
21

Rebuttal Testimony of Information Technology Panel

Q. 
In addition to what you previously described, did the Company 
1

3

4

5

8 
cases and FWBs contain a breakdown of the costs by cost elements (i.e., 
9

10

11

12 
detail including assumptions behind the cost estimates that the Company 
13 
provided in the response to IR DPS-482 Supplemental, which is attached 
14 
as part of Exhibit __ (ITP-1R).  The Company’s response provided a 
15

16

17 
development and the bases and assumptions used to produce the Rate Year 
18 
and Data Year estimates.  The Company also extracted the relevant cost

the responses to IR DPS-396, 399, 403, 404 – 406, and 412.  These 
17 
documents explain the value of each project and discuss any upside and 
18

19 
spreadsheets and the accompanying PowerPoints were provided to 
20 
supplement the sanction papers and FWBs, the information contained in 
21

Q. 
The SITP asserts (at 36) that final project costs often vary widely 
4 
from the Company’s preliminary project estimates and partial 
5

6 
that spending in the Rate Year will likely be very different than the 
7

8

9

10

11

12

14

16

17 
preliminary estimates.  The analysis also shows that the Company’s 
18 
preliminary estimates are generally conservative.  Such conservative 
19 
estimates do not support the reductions in the Company’s CAPEX budgets

recommended by Staff.

20

Q. 
The Staff Security Panel (“SSP”) (at 15-16) recommends that the 
1 
gunshot protection system proposed for the Company’s Syracuse 
2 
facilities be removed from the IT capital budget.  Does the Panel 
3 
agree? 
4 
A. 
No.  National Grid is one of the largest employers in the City of Syracuse, 
5 
with about 1,500 employees/contractors working at the main Syracuse 
6 
Office Complex (“SOC”) at 300 Erie Boulevard West.  The SOC is home 
7 
to a large Customer Call Center that is staffed throughout the day.  The 
8 
proposed gunshot detection systems are planned for the SOC as well as the 
9 
Company’s facilities that house the control center.    
10 
 
11 
 
The proposed gunshot detection systems are intended to enhance safety at 
12 
the SOC and control center facilities.  According to U.S. Federal Bureau 
13 
of Investigation statistics, in 2018 Syracuse had a violent crime rate more 
14 
than double that of New York State as a whole, and almost twice the U.S. 
15 
average.  According to Syracuse Police, there have already been over 200 
16 
more calls of shots fired in the City in 2020 than in all of 2019.   
17 
 
18 
 
Specific to the SOC, the presence of the Customer Call Center further 
19 
supports the need for enhanced protection.  There have been several 
20 
incidents where irate customers have threatened to travel to the SOC to 
21 


--- Page 16 ---
Rebuttal Testimony of Information Technology Panel 
 
 
 
 
14 of 22 
 
commit violence on the facility or to call center employees.  Recent SOC 
1 
lobby security enhancements included hardening of the entrance/reception 
2 
area that limited access to the office areas.  Gunshot detection with 
3 
immediate law enforcement notification is the next step in securing the 
4 
Company’s facilities.  Accordingly, the SSP’s recommendation to remove 
5 
the gunshot protection system from the IT capital budget should be 
6 
rejected.

V. 
SITP Forecasting Adjustment 
9 
Q. 
Please describe the SITP’s proposed IT forecasting adjustment. 
10 
A. 
The SITP recommends a forecasting adjustment that was derived by first 
11 
removing the costs associated with AMI, CIS, VOLT Enablement and 
12 
Grid Modernization projects addressed by other Staff witness panels.  The 
13 
removal of these projects from the Rate Year IT capital spending forecast 
14 
reduces the Service Company’s IT CAPEX forecast from $376.739 
15 
million to $305.153 million.  The SITP then developed a regression-based 
16 
Rate Year IT CAPEX spending level of $174.548 million using a linear 
17 
analysis of the Service Company’s IT spending in the period FY2016-
18 
FY2020.  The SITP then calculated the difference between the adjusted 
19 
forecast of $305.153 million and the regression result of $174.548 million, 
20 
and divided the difference ($130.625 million) by the $305.153 million 
21 


--- Page 17 ---
Rebuttal Testimony of Information Technology Panel 
 
 
 
 
15 of 22 
 
amount to arrive at an adjustment factor of 42.8 percent, which was 
1 
applied to the budgets for all ADMS, Core IT and the Unadjusted Grid 
2 
Modernization and VOLT Enablement projects.  The SITP’s methodology 
3 
results in a recommended IT CAPEX budget of $195.295 million. 
4 
 
5 
Q. 
Does the Company believe it is appropriate to utilize a linear 
6 
regression analysis to determine an IT forecasting adjustment?   
7 
A.  
No.  The SITP forecasting adjustment is a backward-looking analysis that 
8 
completely fails to recognize and give effect to the future needs and 
9 
demands of the Company’s gas and electric business for IT investment.  
10 
The use of information technology is essential to the operation of the 
11 
Company’s electric and gas businesses and the services required by the 
12 
business and offered in the IT market are rapidly changing. This has 
13 
created an environment where the demand for IT service continues to 
14 
grow at much faster pace than in the past.  The SITP’s approach to 
15 
forecasting the need for IT CAPEX in the Rate Year fails to account for 
16 
either the increase in demand for IT enhancements and the organizational 
17 
changes that the IT area has made to improve its’ project delivery 
18 
capabilities.  These changes, which were described at length in our direct 
19 
testimony (at 10-17), include: 
20 
• the implementation of delivery centers; 
21 


--- Page 18 ---
Rebuttal Testimony of Information Technology Panel 
 
 
 
 
16 of 22 
 
• on-boarding of numerous project managers and analysts to deliver 
1 
the programs and projects; 
2 
• adjusting the IT organization’s resourcing model to bring more 
3 
technical expertise back in-house; and  
4 
• the roll-out of a core flex framework that provides the IT area 
5 
with the capability to quickly bring contract resources on-board 
6 
as needed.    
7 
 
8 
The above changes have occurred during the last two years to respond to 
9 
the increase in demand for IT services and the impending start of the 
10 
Transformation initiatives.  The use of a backward-looking tool, such as 
11 
linear regression, to set future spending levels ignores the above realities 
12 
and results in an unreasonably low forecast for Rate Year IT spending.  
13 
 
14 
Q. 
Leaving aside the Panel’s concerns that the Staff forecasting 
15 
adjustment is unreasonably based on a backward-looking analysis, 
16 
are there flaws in the Staff regression analysis that cause it to produce 
17 
an unreasonable result? 
18 
A. 
Yes.  Those flaws are described in greater detail by the Company’s 
19 
Revenue Requirements Panel. 
20 
 
21 


--- Page 19 ---
Rebuttal Testimony of Information Technology Panel 
 
 
 
 
17 of 22 
 
Q. 
How would the SITP’s recommended level of CAPEX spending of 
1 
$195 million in the Rate Year affect the Company’s ability to meet the 
2 
needs of its gas and electric businesses?  
3 
A. 
As also discussed in the rebuttal testimony of the Company’s EIOP and 
4 
GIOP, reductions of the level proposed by the SITP would jeopardize the 
5 
Company’s ability to continue to deliver safe and reliable service to 
6 
customers and unreasonably delay needed upgrades to the computing 
7 
infrastructure.  Adoption of the Staff adjustments will also delay the 
8 
realization of the customer benefits included in the Transformation 
9 
initiatives.  With respect to the Core IT Plan, Staff recommended a Rate 
10 
Year spending level of $132 million, which is well below the Company’s 
11 
forecast of $222 million during the Rate Year.  The recommended 
12 
spending level is also significantly below the current FY 2021 forecast for 
13 
Core IT of $234 million.  It goes without saying that the adjustments 
14 
required to the IT core plans to meet Staff’s proposed reductions would 
15 
have a staggering impact to critical programs such as:  Technology 
16 
Modernization and Cyber Security and many smaller but no less critical 
17 
projects that are funded from the Core IT budget.  The programs and 
18 
projects funded from Core IT include the investments needed to ensure the 
19 
Company’s computing infrastructure remains safe and reliable.  A 42 
20 
percent adjustment would likely result in the cancellation or delay of many 
21 


--- Page 20 ---
Rebuttal Testimony of Information Technology Panel 
 
 
 
 
18 of 22 
 
key programs and add significant risk to the continued operation of many 
1 
of these systems.   
2 
 
3 
Q. 
Would the reduction in the IT CAPEX budget recommended by the 
4 
SITP have any particular impacts on the Company’s ability to 
5 
maintain cybersecurity? 
6 
A. 
Yes.  A reduction in the IT CAPEX budget as recommended by the SITP 
7 
will negatively impact the Company’s Cyber resilience.  The Company’s 
8 
Cyber Security Program follows a risk-based approach in maintaining and 
9 
improving Cyber Security measures, driven by internal and external threat 
10 
intelligence that illustrates the increasing persistence and capability of 
11 
threat actors and underpinned by the Security Risk Framework that 
12 
quantifies the risk and impact of a threat materializing.  A reduction in the 
13 
IT CAPEX budget will prolong the Company’s exposure to identified 
14 
risks and reduce the ability to effectively implement compensating Cyber 
15 
Security controls that improve identification, protection, detection and 
16 
response capabilities through continuous improvement to keep pace with 
17 
emerging threats, and increased threat actor activity, and would hinder the 
18 
Company’s ability to respond to and limit the impact of potential Cyber 
19 
events. 
20 
 
21 


--- Page 21 ---
Rebuttal Testimony of Information Technology Panel 
 
 
 
 
19 of 22 
 
Q. 
The Panel mentioned that the Company’s FY 2021 Core IT budget is 
1 
$234 million.  Is the Company on track to spend this amount? 
2 
A. 
Yes.  The Company expects that actual Core IT spending for FY 2021 will 
3 
range between $230 million and $245 million.  
4 
 
5 
Q. 
Is there a way to address through the ratemaking process the 
6 
possibility that actual IT spending will vary from budgeted spending 
7 
in the Rate Year of these proceedings? 
8 
A. 
Yes.  As the SITP points out, the Company is currently subject to a 
9 
Service Company Rents IT and GBE Program Net Utility Plant and 
10 
Depreciation Expense Reconciliation Mechanism.  This mechanism, 
11 
which currently operates as a downward-only tracking mechanism, was 
12 
adopted under the terms of the Joint Proposal approved in the Company’s 
13 
2017 base rate proceeding in Case 17-E-0238 et al.  While it is the 
14 
Company’s position that a downward-only tracking mechanism should 
15 
only be adopted as part of multi-year rate settlement, the Company would 
16 
not object to adoption in these proceedings of a two-way tracking 
17 
mechanism that would protect both the Company and its customers from 
18 
differences between the actual IT and GBE Program Average Net Utility 
19 
Plant and Depreciation Expense revenue requirement and the level of that 
20 
requirement used to set rates in these proceedings.  Adoption of a two-way 
21 


--- Page 22 ---
Rebuttal Testimony of Information Technology Panel 
 
 
 
 
20 of 22 
 
tracking mechanism would address the SITP’s concerns that the Company 
1 
may underspend its Rate Year CAPEX budget. 
2 
 
3 
Q. 
Please describe the SITP’s methodology for forecasting the 
4 
Company’s IT-related OPEX and RTB costs. 
5 
A. 
As set forth on Exhibit __ (SITP-2), page 5, Staff determined, using 
6 
information provided by the Company in response to IR DPS-1009, that 
7 
the Service Company’s OPEX and RTB costs were, on average, 26 
8 
percent of its actual capital expenditures during the period of FY2016-
9 
FY2020.  Staff applied this percentage to its capital spending forecast for 
10 
the Company’s ADMS, Core IT, Grid Modernization, and VOLT 
11 
Enablement projects.  Thus, the SITP recommended OPEX and RTB costs 
12 
for the Rate Year of $3.556 million, $34.239 million, $3.465 million, and 
13 
$4.118 million for each of these respective projects. 
14 
 
15 
Q. 
Do you agree with the OPEX and RTB adjustment? 
16 
A. 
No. The information provided in response to IR DPS-1009 mistakenly 
17 
indicates that the costs provided include both project OPEX and RTB 
18 
costs; however, they are Project OPEX only.   The RTB costs are moved 
19 
once the project goes live to the IT Operational team responsible for 
20 
managing the project.  Hence, the cost information was Project OPEX 
21 


--- Page 23 ---
Rebuttal Testimony of Information Technology Panel 
 
 
 
 
21 of 22 
 
only.   The Company has updated IR DPS-1009 to include the RTB costs 
1 
and incorporated the results into Staff’s analysis found in Exhibit __ 
2 
(SITP-2).  The updated analysis is provided in Exhibit __ (ITP-2R), and 
3 
indicates a Project OPEX/RTB to CAPEX ratio of 34 percent.  Even based 
4 
on the SITP’s reduced CAPEX recommendations, using this revised 
5 
percentage would increase the SITP’s recommended OPEX and RTB 
6 
costs from the Rate Year for the ADMS, Core IT, Grid Modernization, 
7 
and VOLT Enablement as follows:

10 
 
More significantly however, the Company’s forecast of OPEX and RTB 
11 
costs was based on a project by project review because there are many 
12 
nuances to IT programs and projects that will cause the relationship 
13 
between CAPEX and OPEX costs to vary.  This is particularly true with 
14 
respect to the Transformation initiatives that are planning to utilize 
15

16 
Platform as a Service (PaaS) and employ unique third-party application

support models.  Also, because these programs involve business process 
1 
changes, more extensive change management and training is required to 
2 
ensure benefits realization.  These factors tend to increase OPEX costs and 
3 
further highlight why applying a standard percentage to all programs is not 
4 
appropriate.

Roles
Acronym Summary Rate
Definition
Agile Transformation Office
ATO
87
Business Analyst
BA
Functional
87 Identify problems and opportunities within a company and help assess solution options
Work with business resources to define and document requirements
Ensure requirements cover all aspects of  the affected business processes
Communicate requirements to the downstream delivery teams
Sets up requirements traceability with the corresponding teams including QA, UAT etc.
Reviews Test Plans, Test Scenarios etc. with the corresponding QA teams
Business Partner
BP
Business
204
Business Consultant
BC
Business
112
Data Mgmt
DM
118
Development
Dev
Technical
118 Use programming languages and source code to create software that meets requirements
Assist in detailed Solution Design creation
Conduct unit tests on the code
Write documentation explaining the code
Assist in diagnosing and fixing problems with the code
DevOps
DO
118 Reviews requirements and establishes a DevOps strategy for the project
Onboards teams to leverage Jira for Agile Planning and Confluence for Collaboration
Onboards teams to leverage Bitbucket for Source Code Management and XRay for Test Management
Designs and develops DevOps pipelines using Jenkins, SonarQube (software quality scans), and Artifactory (artifact management)
Designs and developments deployment automation scripts using Ansible
Identifies and diagnoses any work-in-progress issues
Train teams on proper use of DevOps Tools
Enterprise Architect
EA
Functional
138 Creates the roadmap and regulations guiding IT designs and implementation within a business organization
Coordinates and monitors the activities of other units to ensure compliance with the overarching plan
Collaborates with solution architects to provide enterprise solutions that align with the business need
Selects and designs IT products within the enterprise
Infrastructure
I&O
Technical
118 Includes resources who control and monitor network infrastructure, seucrity/firewall settings, on-premises servers, databases, and 
connectivity to SAAS solutions.
Includes resources who deploy code to controlled environments such as UAT & Prod
Manages Admin, User Privileges on the backend
Project Manager
PM
Functional
113 Plans, budgets, oversees, and documents all aspects of project
Works closely with upper management and technical leads ensuring scope of work is understood and managed
Risk mitigation; Escalation; Executive Communication on an as needed basis
Aligning resources to the project deliverables
Quality Engineering Systems
QES
Functional
87 Reviews requirements and establishes a Test strategy for the project

Under US GAAP, non-capitalizable project costs incurred before implementation
are classified as project Opex costs.  RTB costs are operating expenses that are
incurred after implementation.

Assumptions
Given our past experience with Digital initiatives such as OnMyWay and Nucleus, we’ve estimated the Opex costs for the validation and build phases of digital products is 
~5% of what we spend in Capex.  Given the Capex request that allows us to support 2 products per year, we’ve estimated the Opex need to be at $1.5M each FY which 
would cover validation, build as well as the ideation process known as Hack-a-Future. 
Above is a breakdown for two agile team rates which we’ve estimated to have an average size of 14 FTE.  Rate 1 assumes an all National Grid team that has a lot of 
experience ideating, validating and building digital products.  Rate 2 assumes the team is mostly consultants.  Our request is in-between these two costs given the 
pipeline of products, we believe we will still have consultants on some teams, but we aim to build out National Grid’s capability going forward.

Indicative Project Budget from Program
Assumptions:
An F&A study will be done before the start of the investment to ensure a proper application is selected 
for upgrade, it will also determine the proper solution and confirm the costs of the project. The program 
board will adjust the investments within the program to adjust funds and meet the goals of the program.
The application selected will be those that are not scheduled to be replaced by a in-flight or future 
project.  Tactical solutions will be allowed to extend the life of critical applications which have no 
replacement strategy.  
The estimate assumes both limited internal development and purchase of some of the applications 
within the project, the F&A will determine the proper ratio which may cause a shift between labor and 
software costs with the intent of keeping the total costs within line of the investment.  Again the 
program board will oversee the projects within the program to ensure the goals of the program are met.
Description: This investment will upgrade a minor application, within the Operations space, which is nearing end of support.  Applications 
running on end-of-life servers (window 2003/2008/2012), built on technology no longer supported,  or are losing vendor support (for 
application or database version) will be address.   The investment will seek to maximize the elimination of older servers and remediate the 
most critical applications (most at risk).  As part of this investment duplicate systems at end of life will be consolidated reducing redundancy. 
This investment assumes a simple upgrade to a smaller application.  Later investments will need to address larger systems.
Cost in $
Total
Development & Implementation – OPEX
 Development & Implementation – CAPEX 
Although simple upgrades should not require much training, the estimate includes minimal training. 
The estimate assumes a single low end complete set of servers, Dev/Test/Prod/DR.  There will be no hot 
back-up/redundancy and recovery will be lower band SLA.  
The estimate includes limited purchase software as required to support the migration of applications, to 
a newer version or a replacement. 
Like for like server replacement is expected, although the application may be replatformed in the cloud.  
The intent is to keep the application at the same support level, with a similar DR plan.  Under some 
exceptions where a critical application may be moved to a higher support level, or less critical to a lower 
support level. It is believe the refresh should improve overall performance without changing support 
levels.

running on end-of-life servers (window 2003/2008/2012), built on technology no longer supported,  or are losing vendor support (for 
application or database version) will be address.   The investment will seek to maximize the elimination of older servers and remediate the 
most critical applications (most at risk).  As part of this investment duplicate systems at end of life will be consolidated reducing redundancy. 
This investment assumes a simple upgrade to a smaller application.  Later investments will needed to address larger systems.

General Notes
Do not delete rows from Res Alloc tab
just blank out the data if you don't want it
Columns A thru I filled out on a person by person (or role by role) basis
Monthly cells take FTE amounts (ex: person working 50% of the time should be entered as 50; full time assignment is entered as 1)
Daily rate entered should include burdens for NG
Leave Daily Rate empty to allow for resource projections without cost implications (typically used for business resources)

Assumptions:
As the work required within this project is the follow-up to an F&A done in 2019, we will reconfirm the finding from that study and use as baseline for this effort. 
The estimate includes the purchase of hardware and software as required to replicate the existing instance within the CNI space for external availabilty.
The 2 other Pi components (pi Vision & Distribution Pi),  are being covered with Grid Mod. Specifically, this project will implement a replicated reporting environment that can be queried on demand without impacting the performance of the CNI.
Total Cost Variance 
Description: PI is a real-time data historian application with a highly efficient time-series database. The application can efficiently record data 
from process control systems (ex. Distributed Control System - DCS, Programmable PLC) into a compressed time series database. The PI servers 
within the CNI environments were designed to support the control room operations and not the bulk extracts being requested by folks out on 
Corporate.  We have encountered large extracts crashing the servers and impacting operations.  Corporate Pi was added to scope of this IRS 
because of this. The 2 other Pi components (pi Vision & Distribution Pi),  are being covered with Grid Mod. Specifically, this project will 
implement a replicated reporting environment that can be queried on demand without impacting the performance of the CNI (Critical Network 
Infrastructure) instance while honoring NERC critical infrastructure protection (“CIP”) restrictions.  The environment will be used to support the 
Distributed Generation (DG) Planning Portal, DG IOAP Phase 2 screening in addition to other modeling needs.  Additionally, this project will 
provide planning engineers and analysts with additional software tools to better serve the Company’s customers and other Company 
stakeholders

Assumptions:
The estimate includes the purchase software as required to support the migration of applications, to a newer version or a replacement. 
While there is minor development expected, there will be integration focus to several distribution areas within national grid and the connectivity required.
The middleware, and the labor required to build out these points are also included.
Total Cost Variance (Indicative to Budget)
Description: CYME is the software used for load flow analysis on the electric distribution system.  This allows engineers to plan potential impacts 
of interconnection, new system load, and many other planning scenarios.  With the increase in DER applications and the increasingly dynamic 
impacts to the electric network, the Company must enhance its ability to create our planning models more often. 
This investment will continue next in the Company’s migration toward near real-time models that are automatically updated from the GIS 
connected model.   This work will leverage the connect model export components of the Distribution GIS Next Generation project facilitating our 
ability to continue to enhance responsiveness to interconnection requests and provide network data through our DER System Portal (Distributed 
Energy Resources System Portal). 
This will enable the connections of multiple sources to load flow models. This includes, GIS, PI Data, Smart Meters, etc., and provides a formal 
model change process to approve or disapprove alterations to models. It is highly customizable to add or change connections to the models in 
the future., and this functionality will streamline data extractions for the future of planning and the backend to ADMS models.

5890C - Computapole Replacement
Cost in $
Total
Development & Implementation – OPEX
 Development & Implementation – CAPEX 
Description: Computapole is used to manage and deliver several of our inspection programs including wood pole.   The application is very aged 
and out of support from the vendor.   This project will be a follow on to work conducted as part of the VOLT Enablement Program.   The Project 
VOLT Enablement scope seeks to deploy a new inspection system for our transmission and substation assets.  This project will add distribution 
line assets to the new system. enabling the Company to continue to utilize common resources to keep costs down. 
Existing Computapole platform will be obsolete in 3 years, as company that bought Computapole is phasing out to new Hosting solution, that 
typically doesn’t align with CNI.  Existing setup is in CNI and was upgraded to Windows 7 five years ago. Hand held field devices, very old 
architecture. Also, inspections results are reviewed by NY State Regulators every 3 years and if we fail penalties could be incurred.

Total Cost Variance 
5890D - IDS Next Generation Upgrade
Description: IDS (Interruption Disturbance System), enables the tracking and reporting of distribution interruptions and transmission/substation 
disturbances and is integral to the Company’s ability to analyze and report on reliability performance.   This system was first deployed in 1999 
and needs to be upgraded to more modern technology.  Additionally, enhancements to allow for greater data integration with other analysis 
platforms and greater self-serve functionality are part of the proposed work.  An analysis was conducted in 2018, which identified potential 
paths to address these needs.  This investment follows-on that effort.
IDS is an in-house home grown tool written 20 years ago that is used by Transmission (Interruption) and Distribution (Disturbance). 
Its regulatory driven, reporting reliability liabilities for Ma, RI, & NY.  An upgrade was done last year upgrading the Windows server and Oracle 
DB software (and placing DB on its own schema), but not the hardware platform. Also, the user interface needs major improvement as well as 
the backend code. Were also looking for the ability to automate reports specific to dept. needs without having to rely on 3rd party assistance.

RTB of $200k per year is based on an expected 
cost of vendor support for environment, 
integration, hardware support, including 
middleware and database annual maintenance 
and DBA support.  The environment is high 
availability with fall back redundancy due to 
the critical nature of the system.
Assumptions:
The estimate includes the purchase of a small subscription to the Itron SaaS mobile collection cloud as 
required to support the migration of old devices to the new platform as the old devices fail and cannot be 
replaced. 
An F&A study will be done before the start of the investment to confirm the costs and timeline of the 
project. The program board will adjust the investments within the program to adjust funds and meet the 
goals of the program.
The system will be brought under IT support for future upgrades and system support.
This application is assumed to be an Electric and Gas system, but this investment will cover only Electric 
meters. If it is determined within the F&A study that the system is fully shared with all Gas operating 
companies, the investment will be adjustment bring in the new scope to cover Gas meters as well thus 
increasing costs.  Adding Gas would more than double the costs of the project but would also change the 
Allocation of costs, so there may be a net neutral effect on costs to the electric operating companies.
Like for like server replacement is expected, the FCS system runs on load balanced high available 
hardware.  The intent is to keep the application at the same support level, with a similar DR plan.  The 
support level will be reconfirmed as part of this investment.
The estimate includes the purchase of additional database license to support the migration of application, 
the upgrade will also upgrade the version of Oracle, the recurring yearly maintenance costs and DBA costs 
will be reflected within the yearly RTB (Run the Business).
Interfaces will be converted over to the new middleware to ensure the system is completely upgraded.
Although the upgrades should not require much training, the estimate includes training as required for 
the new version.   Also the new mobile collection devices will require configuration and training.
RTB will include the cost of the new Cloud SaaS mobile solution annual subscription.  
The old FCS servers will be decommissioned as part of the investment.
Total Cost Variance (Indicative to Budget)
Description: This investment will upgrade the FCS system to the latest, version of software, upgraded Oracle Database, upgrade the 
interfaces to MuleSoft and move the system to supportable hardware.  The cost and timeline are being confirmed in the F&A study, this 
estimate is based on the latest information from the vendor (Itron).  This is assumed to be an Electric only upgrade, an F&A currently 
underway will determine the complete scope of the effort (which may include all of gas which would effect the total cost and allocation).

Indicative Project Budget from Program
Description: This investment seeks to replace the separate minor systems running within Meter Data Services and consolidate the 
functionality in fewer newer systems.  The old legacy systems are at end of life, the hardware is at risk and support for the applications will 
be ending.  This investment assumes the consolidation of several smaller systems into a single more robust solution,  an F&A study will be 
undertake before the investment to confirm costs and timeline.  The Program Board will adjust the investment as required within the overall 
Program to meet the goals of the program.
Cost in $
Total
Development & Implementation – OPEX
 Development & Implementation – CAPEX 
Total Cost Variance (Indicative to Budget)
Assumptions:
An F&A study will be done before the start of the investment to ensure a proper applications are selected 
for upgrade, it will also determine the proper solution and confirm the costs of the project. The program 
board will adjust the investments within the program to adjust funds and meet the goals of the program.
The applications selected will be those that are not scheduled to be replaced by a in-flight or future 
project.  Tactical solutions will be allowed to extend the life of critical applications which have no 
replacement strategy.  
The estimate includes the purchase software as required to support the migration of applications, to a 
newer version or a replacement. 
Like for like server replacement is expected, although the application may be re-platformed in the cloud.  
The intent is to keep the application at the same support level, with a similar DR plan.  Under some 
exceptions where a critical application may be moved to a higher support level, or less critical to a lower 
support level. It is believe the refresh should improve overall performance without changing support 
levels.
The estimate includes the purchase of database license to support the migration of applications, the 
recurring yearly maintenance costs and DBA costs will be reflected within the yearly RTB (Run the 
Business).
The estimate assumes both devotement and purchase of some of the applications within the project, the 
F&A will determine the proper ratio which may cause a shift between labor and software costs with the 
intent of keeping the total costs within line of the investment.  Again the program board will oversee the 
projects within the program to ensure the goals of the program are met.
Although simple upgrades should not require much training, the estimate includes training as required or 
new version with new functionality and new replacements.

RTB is based on an expected cost of vendor 
support for integration, hardware support, 
including middleware along with additional 
database license maintenance. Increase infield 
force help desk calls.
Note: A 15-20% RTB is expect as normal for a 
new system implementation, a SaaS solution 
would expect a much higher RTB.
It is estimated that 8 Interfaces will be required 
to be modified and rewritten.
Although the application will ride on the OMW platform an additional database server, application server, 
and web server will be added to the pool of servers supporting OMW to handle the increase workload.
Additional Database Licenses will be required due to the introduction of the new DB server.
There will be approx. 200 mobile trouble worker utilizing the new platform.
Assumptions:
This investment will attempt to utilize the recently developed On My Way (OMW) solution as the platform 
for development, leveraging the database, application and servers.  While adding new screens, order type 
functionality and database values to the system to accommodate MWork fields.
Existing MWork interfaces will be rewritten in MuleSoft and modified to point to the OMW application to 
allow work creation from CSS and completion back to CSS (Customer Systems).  Interfaces to Storms will 
utilize the Storms to Mwork interfaces for scheduling and work completion.  The OMW system will be 
modified to use these interfaces.
New ONW functionality - OMW today creates work based on an interface from the Storms system, it will 
be modified to also create new work directly from CSS. This will require new field which storms does not 
carry today, along with passing completion information back to CSS.  OMW will be enhanced to allow 
interaction with multiple initiating and completion system, by introducing the concept of source system 
ownership of order (as MWork was done). 
OMW reporting will be modified to store the new information and allow additional reporting. 
Total Cost Variance 
Description: Mobile Workforce (Mwork) is a legacy application which supports both Gas and Electric field crews, the Gas crews will be 
moving off the system with the implementation of GBE, which will leave the Electric Trouble crews as the sole users of the old application.  
With most of the servers at end of life, they cannot be decommissioned until the electric trouble crews move to a new system.  This 
investment seeks to move the users over to a new solution and allow the old MWork server to be retired. MuleSoft will be the assumed 
integration software for the new solution.

database.  A determination will need to be made as part of design on recovery  servers.  The servers will be 
virtualized for easy expansion.  The plan would be to share sever load, but the F&A study may move to a 
separation strategy to simply future upgrades.
The estimate assumes both devotement and purchase of some of the applications within the project, the 
F&A will determine the proper ratio which may cause a shift between labor and software costs with the 
intent of keeping the total costs within line of the investment.  Again the program board will oversee the 
projects within the program to ensure the goals of the program are met.

INVP 4408: Document Management 
System Replacement
4408
Document Management 
System Replacement 
This investment will provide a secure and reliable 
enterprise wide Document Management System 
(DMS) that the gas and electric business needs to 
support National Grid’s assets. 
- Provides a platform for the gas and electric 
engineering business to store and retrieve their 
key documents
- The Gas Systems Engineering Risk Register 
carries item #6 “Inability to create, update, 
revise, and access as-built drawings for gas 
transmission mains and regulator stations. This 
project addresses the item on the risk log.
- This is an inflight project from FY20
- Costs are for 4/1/2020 and beyond
- Specifics on the cost are in the Financial Workbook
- Hardware and software costs were incurred in FY20 or prior
- Project expected to go-live in June 2020 and close by October 
2020
- Remaining project costs entered from Dec 2019 forecasts

Gas Storm Hardening Using

INVP 4898: Asset and Work 
Management System for LNG
4898
Asset and Work 
Management System for 
LNG
The LNG Department has been cited on several 
occasions by various auditors for not having an 
automated Maintenance Management System 
(MMS). Therefore, there is a desire within the LNG 
Department to implement an asset and work 
management. Such programs contains modules 
that are specifically designed for both the gas and 
oil industries for deficiency and audit  tracking.
The current LNG maintenance system is comprised 
primarily of spreadsheets and plant specific access 
databases.
- With the implementation of a corporate asset 
management system, all of the information will 
be consolidated into one location.
- Asset management and preventative 
maintenance procedures will be standardized 
across plants.
- This is an inflight project from FY20
- Costs are for 4/1/2020 and beyond
- 12 plants and 25 - 30 asset categories, each may have many 
records (thousands?)
- Assumes 50-75 concurrent users (budget for 100 users)
- Assumes the use of Maximo as the software, no RFP needed
- Assumes this project would be an enhancement to the GBE 
implementation of Maximo and will use the same instance
- Process standardization and data standardization will be 
business responsibility
- Specifics on the costs are in the Financial Workbook
- Expected go-live in August 2021 and close November 2021
- Remaining project costs entered from Dec 2019 forecasts

INVP 5785: Gas Operational Excellence 
Program
5785B
Digital Hub Experience
Teams in the National Grid (NG) business (Gas) are 
piloting an application toolkit called Unity 3D 
(unity.com) to host their daily Hub (staff huddles to 
analyze/improve field operations) meetings. This 
is a very common mobile App Development Kit and 
Integrated Development Environment (IDE). The 
App runs on a mobile device or on a laptop that 
displays the data on a large-screen monitor.
- This provides interactivity to help orchestrate
and run the team Hub.
- Currently, the application has no integration 
with any other NG system.
- The purpose of this effort is to extend this
functionality across all NG (US) sites and 
potentially provide integration to corporate 
data stores and Key Performance Metrics (KPI's).
- 10 Unity 3D development licenses @ 2.5k/license = $25k
- 5 servers @ 10k per server = $50k

INVP 5787: Gas Foundation for Future

5787A
Gas Control Center 
Simulator
Previously INVP 5470 and 5788B:
National Grid (NG) has Gas Control Centers in MA 
and NY to operate the transmission and 
distribution networks across the US gas service 
territory. Gas Control is regulated under Pipeline 
and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration 
(PHMSA) Control Room Management Regulations 
(CFR 192.631) to provide extensive controller 
training as well as simulation training to the 
operators responsible for operating our networks. 
NG is currently meeting these requirements via 
paper-driven table-top drills and meetings. NG has 
experienced a large turnover of operators in the 
past 3-5 years with another wave expected to occur 
This project provides NG a platform to 
modernize our Gas Control Training Program to 
an industry leading computer-driven simulation 
solution.
- Sole source approach with the existing SCADA vendor
- This will be a CNI hosted application
- Estimates based on prior details in the Financial Workbook

Recovery Time Objective (RTO ) agreed along with 
the business application owner. No Investment 
initiatives in FY21-25 roadmap are identified to

gas applications that will need to be covered by 
this initiative :
App ID 1116.000: Synergee  (DBA Support)
App ID 2272.000: Endpoint Processing System (EPS)
App ID 1109.000: SNAP
App ID 1162.000: eLogger (DBA Support only) Gas
App ID xxxx.xxx: QTS (Gas) Database
- Less outage time on those applications
- No/very few BCP required
- Project covers only DR for applications that will not be retired
by GBE or by App Rat efforts
- Servers and DB  will NOT need to upgraded to the highest 
version that the current version of the application supports, 
since that is covered by a different project. 
- DR framework exists for current deployment but the
applications don't subscribe to it
- This is a DR implementation and not HA
- Assuming 2 months per application(5)
- No changes to interfaces
- No automated testing tools
- No change to OS (i.e.. AIX to Linux, Windows to MacOS, etc.)
- SQL Server licenses are included with Windows or we have an 
ELA for SQL Server

- 20 licenses x 1k/license = $0.02M

5785H
Residential Methane 
Detection (RMD) Inbound 
Feed and Actioning F&A
Previously INVP 5161:
National Grid (NG) is exploring the possibility of 
getting electronic data feeds from 3rd party 
Residential Methane Detection (RMD) vendors, 
such that such IOT devices installed at customer 
premises can alert National Grid to high levels of 
methane at customer sites
- NG could react to such alerts and 
automatically dispatch Customer Meter Services 
(CMS) First-Responders to the Customer 
premises, without the need for customers to 
have to call NG.
- Feasibility & Analysis (Proof of Concept) project to test the 
ability to receive inbound methane detection feeds from 
companies such as Nest, Ring etc. 
- If successful, a follow up project would be set up to 
productionalize this set up
- F&A would be set up in a lab within any NG location

customers and processes to the Gas 
Transportation Information System, that went 
live in 2016. Included in the investment is a 
technology upgrade required by GTIS to support 
the additional workload, and provide GTIS with 
upgrades to its .NET environment and browser 
support.  System enhancements will include 
integration with pipeline Electronic Data 
Interchange (EDI) automating the Nomination/ 
- Costs based on option to "Deploy GTIS to all Regions"
- Estimates from Doug McCarthy and his prior research with IBM, 
Wipro, Service Delivery, etc.
- Assumes decommissioning of:
UNY TSA and UNY EBB DWH
RI TSA and RI EBB DWH
MA BMS/CMCS and MA EBB DWH

INVP 5788: Gas Pipeline Safety and 
Compliance Program
5788C
Gas Application Lifecycle 
Management (ALM) 
This project is aimed at upgrading various servers 
in the US NG Data Centers that have either not 
been upgraded for years and/or have not been 
patched due to the inability to patch the older 
versions of the operating systems. This is causing a 
huge security risk to National Grid and its 
operations and needs to be addressed in FY21. 
This project focuses on the servers required to be 
upgraded/patched for US Gas.
The following gas application are proposed to be 
upgraded to more recent servers before GBE finally 
rolls out:
- Cascade Gas
- RMVRT
- SNAP 
- DIS
- Gas Sales Proposals (GSP)
- Gas T Readings Entry System
- Public Building DB/Fixed Factor DB
- Portal for ArcGIS  
- Paving DB, Pave Seed, Restoration DB
- NGA Gas Operations School Certificates
- NRG
In addition to that, those gas applications will be 
decomissioned and the servers will potentially be
freed up:
- combustible gas indicator test (cgi) (pcad)
(pragmacad)
- Risk: Exposure to security risk since server 
cannot benefits for vendor patch (obsolete 
Operating System, software version too further 
away…)
- Risk: Longer business outage (application that 
could not be restarted…)
- Less application outages: Reduction of P1/P2
- Project covers only servers for applications that will not be
retired by GBE or by App Rat efforts
- Servers, OS'es, DB's, and applications  will need to upgraded to
the highest version that the current version of the vendor 
supports.
- No significant changes to interfaces
- No automated testing tools
- No switch of OS (i.e.. AIX to Linux, Windows to MacOS, etc.)
- SQL Server licenses are included with Windows or we have an 
ELA for SQL Server
- 20 servers x 20k/server = $0.400M
- 20 licenses x 1k/license = $0.020M
- 10 Oracle DB licenses x 10k/license = $0.100M
- 10 applications x 150k/license = $1.500M

Enhance Long Island 
GIS/Mapping Data to Be 
Consistent With 
Digital/Geospatial Format
1. Vectorize all raster data (drawings) for Long
Island
2. Revise current landbase with one that has sub-
meter accuracy 
3. Conflate all legacy LI GIS data to the new
landbase
This investment will correct the spatial data 
inaccuracies of all LI GIS data
- Allow NG to use GPS technology to track
underground assets.
- Additionally, this will allow NG to correctly 
overlay external GIS data from contractors, 
partners (electric/telephone/sewer companies), 
government agencies, etc.
- This project will be executed after GBE migration of the NRG GIS
to Esri
- The project revolves around digitizing the raster data in the 
Long Island (LI) NRG GIS System and scanned service records to
vector format
- The data would have to be QA/QC'd by internal staff in Maps & 
Records, before they are imported into the Esri GIS system and 
then published to end-users in the field
- Vendor Vectorization Cost: Map tiles = 33,000 @ $100 per tile =
$3.3M
- Vendor Vectorization Cost: Scanned Service Records =  450,000 @
$10 per service = $4.5M
- Internal NG Vectorization QA/QC Cost to validate 33,000 tiles = 9 
FTE's = 5 FTE's over 2 years
- 1 FTE can QA/QC 2 map tile in 1 hr. Therefore 1 FTE can QA/QC 2 *
160 * 12 images in 1 yr. Therefore, 33,000 images can be QA / QC'd 
by 33000/(2 * 160*12) = 8.59 FTE's (approx. 9 FTE's) = approx. 5 
FTE's over 2 years.
- 1 FTE can QA/QC 10 service cards in 1 hr. Therefore 1 FTE can 
QA/QC 10 * 160 * 12 images in 1 yr. Therefore, 450,000 images can 
be QA / QC'd by 450000/(10 * 160*12) = 23.4 FTE's (approx. 24 FTE's)
= approx. 12 FTE's over 2 years.
- Internal NG Vectorization QA/QC Cost to validate 450,000

INVP 5785: Gas Operational Excellence 
Program
x
Redraw the NYC 
Intersection (ID) Drawings 
onto the World Map for a 
Fully Connected Map for 
NYC
Redraw NYC intersection maps (approx. 32,000) onto 
vector layer.
This investment will support a fully connected 
network model with vector details of GIS data at 
each intersection.
- This project will be executed after GBE migration of the NRG GIS
to Esri
- This project involves digitizing the intersection drawings (ID)
files from TIF/RLC raster format to Esri vector format
- The next step in the project would involve georeferencing and 
linking the rasters images to intersection points in the Esri GIS
system being deployed by GBE
- All of the above would be done by a vendor that has expertise
in heads-up digitizing and geofencing
- The last step in the process would be to import the data into
the Gas GIS system
- Cost of vectorizing and georeferencing 32000 ID files @ $100 per 
file = 32000*100 = $3.2M
- Internal NG Vectorization QA/QC Cost to validate 32,000 tiles =
17 FTE's
- 1 FTE can QA/QC 1 image in 1 hr. Therefore 1 FTE can QA/QC 1 * 
160 * 12 images in 1 yr. Therefore, 32,000 images can be QA / QC'd
by 32000/(160*12) = 16.6 FTE's (approx. 17 FTE's)
- 2 FTE's to run automated QA checks and import the data

devices in the field, before T1 technology is 
decommissioned by the providers.
-This project will be executed by Mike Benedicto
- Total estimated cost~ 5M from Mike B
- Potentially needs ARB and Security alignment and approval

Application Rationalization 
(FY22 and Beyond)
After GBE rolls out, a set of gas applications can be 
decommissioned after a quarantine / read only 
period. Once that period is over, the project will 
take care of archiving the data and retiring the IT 
ecosystems (Servers, maintenance, licenses…).
- Reduction in Data Center complexity
- Simplification of ecosystem environment from 
the support point of view
- Reduction in Run-the-Business (RTB) costs 
resulting from reduction of software licenses, 
hardware maintenance, and application 
support :  from couple ten thousand k$/year in 
FY21 to 500k$/year in FY24.
- Number of applications to be decommissioned is expected to
be approximately the following counts over a 5 year period 
starting FY21:
FY21: 5
FY22: 10
FY23: 20
FY24: 10
FY25: 10
- Assumes that the archival system is already in place and the 
effort is purely to get business approval to decommission the 
application and archive the application/data in its raw format (if
needed for future use)
- No data extraction/conversion costs are assumed
- No software purchases and associated licenses are expected
- $25K per application (labor to seek approvals and working with

Tim Bishton

Assurance
INV 5910 Group Group 
Functions Regulatory / 
Mandated Requests
Efficiency, Reliability and Costs
Run
In 2018, National Grid defined its vision and strategic roadmap to enable a collaborative enterprise approach to governance, risk 
and compliance (GRC) programmes across its multiple operations.
The enablement technology is RSA Archer system, a market leading solution enterprise governance, risk and compliance (eGRC) 
and initial implementation included SOx Controls, Corporate Audit and DR&S for SOx.
Further phasing in 2018 includes Enterprise Risk Management and other compliance  processes for a broader integration.
This project will deliver the continued  investments required  during the life of the asset / contract to maximise business value 
from overall investment benefiting from the continued enhancement to the product in line with industry changes.
(Note consolidation of INVP T20004 Corporate Risk & Compliance)
Asset Health
Leveraging eGRC technology enables;
Improved monitoring
Improved real-time enhanced reporting
Automation driving more efficient workflow
Reduction in errors eliminating manual process
Improved timely decision making
Expanded access to centralised data providing transparency to 
key data across risk and compliance functions reducing 
redundant activities
Simplified and rationalised business and techology architecture
Technology plays an integral role to enabling the business to 
manage GRC programmes with an integrated, standardised and 
consistent approach  managing risk and compliance assurance 
activities efficiently and effectively.
Reverting to historical siloed approach will result in;
Cultural:  Siloed governance over GRC processes and reported 
through multiple risk and compliance committees throughout 
with varying level of participation from impacted stakeholders. 
Summary of key results and issues are shared with relevant 
parties as a point in time view of organization Lacking real-time

INV 5910 Group Group

Efficiency, Reliability and Costs
Run
This project will deliver changes and improvements for Global HR function to ensure effective and efficient operation of the 
Global HR systems. This includes minor works efforts for ;
Service and business improvement enhancements and maintenance
Regulatory or legal policy changes for compliance
This investment will mature following HR Capability
-Manage HR Information Systems
-Develop and Implement Workforce Strategy and Policies
Service Improvements
There is a continuous need for minor application changes, 
service improvement activities and regulatory/legal compliance 
requirements to ensure that corporate applications operate 
effectively and efficiently within respective business processes 
maintaining policy compliance
The impact of doing nothing for regulatory, legal and policy 
compliance drivers has several risks including reputational 
damage, legal action and regulatory fines and penalties. 
Sanctioning small scale changes as individual projects will be a 
higher cost to the business, furthermore there is a risk of not 
being able to mobilise quick enough to meet demand deadlines.

INVP T20046
SuccessFactors (MyHub) Upgrade and Enhancements [Opex]
Corporate
Celeste Schneider
Value Add
HR
INV 5910 Group Group 
Functions Regulatory / 
Mandated Requests
Business Enablement and Customer Satisfaction
Run
In 2018, National Grid  will deliver its strategic roadmap to achieve a significant step improvement in the way  HR processes are 
managed across National Grid, with an ambition to modernise technology to improve the management of data, and the way we 
interact and communicate with our customers and employees for an improved and engaging experience.
The enablement technology is SAP Success Factors Employee Central, a market leading integrated suite of human capital 
management (HCM) web-based applications which will serve as the organisations central system of record.
This capital project will deliver the replacement for required capabilities in line with the asset refresh as set out in the contract 
schedule for SAP Successfactors and builds on the foundations laid during RIIO T1 period.
Asset Health
Increased focus and investment on our people processes and 
supporting systems is a strategic imperative and will yield 
significant benefits through technology enablement;
1. Simple global people processes based on common HR 
business services
2. Enabling data driven decisions by the business, based on a 
single reliable source of data
3. Reduced central costs through the increase of direct access
4. Transparency of HR services and costs giving visibility of the
value of HR to our customers
5. Improved scalability for both Mergers & Acquisition and 
Divestment
6. Ability to access anywhere, anytime including mobile
7. Rich management information enabling National Grid to see
how the organisation is using people processes and 
improvements
8. Simplifying our people processes will release capacity for our 
line managers
Note: SaaS subscription also includes software maintenance 
upgrades and functional enhancements.  We have allocated 
OpEx budget to test the larger maintenance upgrades and for
exploitation of relevant new functionality.
Technology plays an integral role to enabling the business deliver 
its current and future objectives.
1.  No trusted system containing ‘single version of the truth’
2. Processes too cumbersome and complex for users
3. Limited visibility of clear process demand, service standards
and cost transparency
4. Limited ability to consistently produce meaningful and accurate
analytics and KPIs
5.  Multiple data sources required to support regulatory
submissions
6. Key gaps relating to certain data e.g. Position, Contingent 
Workers
7. Multiple access channels resulting in a poor experience for user
Achievement of business priorities will demand a robust and 
innovative HR strategy informed by a deep understanding of the 
21st Century workforce.  The strategy is enabled by the
technologies that provide a foundation for standardised processes
and capabilities informed by the latest thinking in industry .

INVP T20046
SuccessFactors (MyHub) Upgrade and Enhancements [Capex]
Corporate
Celeste Schneider
Value Add
HR
INV 5910 Group Group 
Functions Regulatory / 
Mandated Requests
Business Enablement and Customer Satisfaction
Run
In 2018, National Grid  will deliver its strategic roadmap to achieve a significant step improvement in the way  HR processes are 
managed across National Grid, with an ambition to modernise technology to improve the management of data, and the way we 
interact and communicate with our customers and employees for an improved and engaging experience.
The enablement technology is SAP Success Factors Employee Central, a market leading integrated suite of human capital 
management (HCM) web-based applications which will serve as the organisations central system of record.
This capital project will deliver the replacement for required capabilities in line with the asset refresh as set out in the contract 
schedule for SAP Successfactors and builds on the foundations laid during RIIO T1 period.
Asset Health
Increased focus and investment on our people processes and 
supporting systems is a strategic imperative and will yield 
significant benefits through technology enablement;
1. Simple global people processes based on common HR 
business services
2. Enabling data driven decisions by the business, based on a 
single reliable source of data
3. Reduced central costs through the increase of direct access
4. Transparency of HR services and costs giving visibility of the
value of HR to our customers
5. Improved scalability for both Mergers & Acquisition and 
Divestment
6. Ability to access anywhere, anytime including mobile
7. Rich management information enabling National Grid to see
how the organisation is using people processes and 
improvements
8. Simplifying our people processes will release capacity for our 
line managers
Technology plays an integral role to enabling the business deliver 
its current and future objectives. 
1. No trusted system containing ‘single version of the truth’
2. Processes too cumbersome and complex for users
3. Limited visibility of clear process demand, service standards
and cost transparency
4. Limited ability to consistently produce meaningful and accurate
analytics and KPIs
5. Multiple data sources required to support regulatory
submissions
6. Key gaps relating to certain data e.g. Position, Contingent 
Workers
7. Multiple access channels resulting in a poor experience for user
Achievement of business priorities will demand a robust and 
innovative HR strategy informed by a deep understanding of the 
21st Century workforce. The strategy is enabled by the
technologies that provide a foundation for standardised processes
and capabilities informed by the latest thinking in industry .
Y
Headcount : UK - 33% ; US - 66%

INVP T20057
Legal Support Systems [Capex]
Corporate
Mo Ajaz
Value Add
Legal
INV 5910 Group Group 
Functions Regulatory / 
Mandated Requests
Efficiency, Reliability and Costs
Run
National Grid consistently develop, implement and negotiate a variety of contract types across the organisation.
Contract automation capability will provide National Grid will the ability to automate and self service the contract lifecycle from 
intake to management including the creation and drafting stage which can be time consuming an inefficient.
By adopting a contract automation solution many contact types will be able to be automated, resulting in a streamlined and 
efficent process and reducing the support required from business units such as Legal.
Furthermore, contract automation will provide NG will the ability to create contract template libraries where there will be a 
consistent and standardised approach to contract creation and generation.
Additionally,  over the financial year of 17/18 NG Legal have implemented the use of matter management to be able to 
consolidate all legal matter related documentation used by internal and external stakeholder.
During the RIIO T2 period, there will need to be a refresh and upgrade of this solution which would involve, procuring a new 
solution at a cheaper cost with the same functionality or to remain with the same system and expand its functionality in line 
with the vendors IT functionality roadmap.
RTB reduction
Reductions of time takes to develop contract draft.
Consistent template design of all in house contract types.
Reduction of support required from Legal for contact 
development.
Business self-service capability.
Consolidation of contract types and newly generation contracts
Potential for integration with contract management lifecycle 
tooling.
Assessment to see if we can reduce the spend of the IT tooling.
Expansion of capability and functionality.
Improved workflow, automation and efficiency.
Reduced spend.
By not adopting contract automation capability and functionality 
National Grid will continue to work in the same way.
Not working in line with the National Grid Strategy of finding a 
better way.
Process inefficiency as the time take for contract development is 
time consuming.
Business reliance on supporting business area such as legal for 
contract review resulting in spend wastage.
Siloed approach to template design, with inconsistent processes 
and a lack of centralised visibility on contract generation.
The risk of not going through a refresh and upgrade would be:
Working in a inefficient manner in line with new technology 
capability.
Not working in line with the national grid IT digital strategy.
Wasted support and licencing cost.
Lack of new capability and functionality to reduce OpEx for the 
customer.

INVP T20061

Corporate
Alison Robinson
Value Add
Other
INV 5910 Group Group 
Functions Regulatory / 
Mandated Requests
Efficiency, Reliability and Costs

This Minor works project will enable the corporate applications to run effectively and allow the organisation to respond quickly 
and efficiently to ad-hoc demands and change requests which typically arise when there is either:
An urgent mandatory imperative - e.g. statutory change required by SOX or similar requirements.
A minor change with a high level of business or service improvement
Service Improvements
There is a continuous need for minor application changes, 
service improvement activities and regulatory/legal compliance 
requirements to ensure that corporate applications operate 
effectively and efficiently within respective business processes 
maintaining policy compliance
The impact of doing nothing for regulatory, legal and policy 
compliance drivers has several risks including reputational 
damage, legal action and regulatory fines and penalties. 
Sanctioning small scale changes as individual projects will be a 
higher cost to the business, furthermore there is a risk of not 
being able to mobilise quick enough to meet demand deadlines.

INVP T20001
Data Analytics & Visualisation 
[Capex]
Corporate
Tim Bishton/Alison Kay
Value Add
Assurance, Audit & Legal
INV 5909 Group Group 
Function Operational 
Excellence
Business Enablement and Customer Satisfaction
Grow
Strategic data analytics & visualisation tooling will be required across business units within NG to enable senior 
executives to obtain real time reporting insights by pulling and consolidating data from multiple strategic project, 
programmes and platform in a single view.
We will need this capability to bolster our strategic Governance, Risk & Compliance programme to provide our 
Leadership team with real time reporting and visualisation of corporate risk, assurance and audit requirements, actions 
and outcomes. This capability will also provide leadership to examine and analysis historic data for pattern recognition 
and remediation planning.
Similarly, another example of this need will be required by our Legal Team, developing capability of our 'matter' and 
'spend' tracking systems.
The legal sector is fast changing and with investments in data analytics NG will be able to exploit in house historical case 
data combined with legal precedents to deliver case insights, trends and patterns which would have been previously 
missed.
Legal analytical solutions will enable NG to avoid the need to outsource work to panel firms or extensive use of paralegal 
service.
By investing in this technology, NG legal will be continuing to promote efficiency and cost saving activities over RIIO T2 
period.
Business improvement
Audit, SoX control and Legal teams are both high profile 
and critical areas in which the exec management teams are 
very interested. Effective communication of the holistic and 
co-ordinated assurance landscape is essential for 
transparency and growth in governance and control.
To overcome limited and imperfect data displays from the 
system we need diverse and flexible reporting with minimal 
manual intervention. We have already had to build excel 
macros off the back of the system to overcome some of 
these limitations.
We cannot meet Senior Executive management expectations 
in terms of reporting quality and insight.
We will not realise the full benefits of the new system 
because we will not achieve assurance reporting across the 
organisation which leverages deep insight from the data held 
in the system nor will we achieve co-ordinated assurance 
plans and reporting.
Adopting new technology within National Grid Legal will 
ensure that the organisation will be able operate effectively 
and efficiently, working in line with the RIIO T2 objective and 
National Grid strategy to find a better way. By not adopting 
these new technologies the risk to be business will be:
-Continued spend outsourcing to external panel firms.
-Continued inefficiencies with sourcing to external panel
firms.
-Lack of in house capability for complex legal case work due to
the continued need of simple research activities.
-Siloed approach and methodology to case by case needs.
-Lack of centralised data mining.
Y
Headcount : UK - 50% ; US - 50%

INVP T20037
Case Management [Capex]
Corporate
Claire Jenkins
Value Add
HR
INV 5909 Group Group 
Function Operational 
Excellence
Efficiency, Reliability and Costs
Run
HR case management capability will require a refresh in line contract renewals. This investment will ensure HR are able 
to grow and expand capability related to employee case related concerns.
There are many elements to the functionality that need to be address from a business perspective including process and 
workflow automation, document storage, system intergration, demand management and reporting capability along with 
compliance in relation to GDPR.
From Employee experience perspective, potential strategic option that will be investigated will be - SNOW
This investment will mature following HR Capability

INVP T20043
Digitising Learning [Opex]
Corporate
Claire Jenkins
Value Add
HR
INV 5909 Group Group 
Function Operational 
Excellence
Business Enablement and Customer Satisfaction
Grow
To support the achievement of National Grid’s strategic priorities and vision we need to ensure that we have the right 
skills, knowledge and people capability. We require an approach to learning that is agile to meet the needs of the 
organization now and in the future. Our goal is to be a leading learning organisation, embracing the benefits of 
technology and flexible approaches to learning. This requires continuous  assessment of the effectiveness, efficiency and 
strategic value impact of our learning approach and adapt accordingly.
Our goal is to provide high quality development opportunities for our employees which is essential for us to construct, 
maintain and operate our electric and gas networks safely and reliably.
This investment is required to implement the required actions to enhance both the technical and professional abilities of 
our employees to continually improve performance for the business and close any capability gaps.
Service Improvements
Building a competent workforce is becoming increasingly 
critical as well as the importance of effective technical 
operations and leadership and capability training.  In order 
to deliver measurable business improvements, an increase 
in investment (people/resources including technology) is a 
necessity to close the gap between the criticality of 
Operations and Corporate training that delivers value to 
the business.
The use of technology- based training solutions is essential 
in decreasing the cost of training while increasing the speed 
of a competent employee.  On-the-job technology support 
is an effective training tool and a valuable asset in gaining 
business support and investment.  Additionally, new 
technologies will increase improvements in productivity.  
Investments in e-Learnings, mobile learning, social learning 
and virtual learning should be made to effectively deliver 
training, store and to communicate knowledge. It is critical 
that future technology solutions can be used that are agile 
to meet changing demands.
The most common areas that are placing increased pressure 
on learning and development include an aging workforce, 
millennial workforce, aging infrastructure/grid modernization, 
new technologies, regulatory requirements, operational cost 
pressures and cost pressures on training.    It is imperative 
that we have the right skills, knowledge and people capability. 
Training the workforce is most critical to improve workforce 
safety and compliance while optimizing business performance 
metrics.  Investing in employees’ technical, professional 
development and leadership and capabilities education is vital 
to maximizing workforce potential and maximizing 
stakeholder value delivering services in the most effective and 
efficient way

2. Stops the need to create papers packs for board 
meetings.
3. Expanding the usage of the platforms capability  will 
remove the need to send emails and request for approaval, 
ensuring all board communication are stored in one
location.

National Grid Board reverting back to the pervious ways of 
working, Preparing and printing paper pack, taking more time.
This will lead to long time periods of circulating information 
and could pose a threat to a potential leak of information 
with all of the emails and paper with duplicated information.
A data/information leak at the board level could have a 
catastropic impact to National Grid from a reputational, 
financal and legal stand point.

Description :
Benefits :
Main Driver :
Cost Estimate Assumptions :
 (ie Vendor quote, RFP results, 
Industry benchmarks)
The scope of this initiative includes all aspects of lifecycle management of the Service Now platform including: managing and performing the upgrading and mitigation process 
to remain in support compliance, testing and validating new capabilities associated with the platform and monitoring and tuning the system to ensure it is performing 
optimally.
The Service Now platform provides significant business value and benefit by driving automated workflows, providing service management capabilities and housing internal 
service catalogs.  Keeping the platform refreshed on supported versions is critical to ensuring full availability and use of the platform.
Each updated version of Service Now also includes new features, functions and capabilities that unlock new opportunities to further maximize the system value to the business.  
The rate of business of adoption and utilization of Service Now grows each year given the automated workflow capabilities the system has to offer which increases the business 
and end user experience and reduces overall operating costs.
Service Now is a widely used strategic platform within National Grid.   This investment will ensure the proper number of system upgrades and optimizations are completed 
each year so National Grid can remain on supported service and can maximize the benefits of use of the platform by IT and the business.
National Grid has previously upgraded Service Now and the effort has been in the $200K-$300K per upgrade.   Additional platform enhancement and improvement work is 
typically in the $100K - $300K range depending on the level of effort and complexity of the enhancement.  The strategic plan is to implement between 1 and 2 upgrades per 
year and to implement between 1 and 3 platform enhancement capabilities each year.

Description :
Benefits :
Main Driver :
Cost Estimate Assumptions :
 (ie Vendor quote, RFP results, 
Industry benchmarks)
 This program will fund projects to support, enhance, and replace IT Middleware. In the current application landscape, there is an increasing need to enable  applications to 
exchange data to better facilitate business processes and communicate with external partners. This ability to exchange information has become critical to many processes and 
applications. The current platforms are at or nearing maximum capacity for their current design. Each of these toolsets and the infrastructure platforms hosting them are 
currently out of support or will be out of support by the end of the calendar year 2020.   To address new and changed integration requirements, the Oracle Fusion Middleware 
(OFM) platform has been placed in containment by Enterprise Architecture (EA) and MuleSoft has been selected by EA as the new integration platform.   A minimum of three 
phases have been identified to address the migration of services to Mulesoft
 Introduction of modern integration capabilities utilizing current technology. 
Implementation of additional capacity in the middleware suite. 
Improved resiliency of the integration platform. 
Improved supportability and skills availability. 
Risk mitigation of the current integration environment. 
A flexible environment that can grow as business needs increase. 
Use of cloud ready integration platform. 
Reduction of technical debt. 
Simplified adoption by IT and Business organizations.
The immediate need is to remove risks associated with Oracle Fusion Middleware / Service Oriented Architecture (OFM/SOA).  In parallel, future years investments will be 
prioritized.
Cost estimates are based on similar historical projects and the estimating guidelines in the Solution Delivery Framework.  Software costs reflect additional Mulesoft license 
requirements to support each phase of the migration.
Cost Assumptions: 
- Capex: Labor/Other/Hardware/Software split is  60/10/5/25
- Opex:   Labor/Other split is 90/10

2
Investment Overview 
The Upstate New York, Massachusetts, and Rhode Island Gas Supply and Retail Choice 
programs are supported by these legacy applications:  

Electronic Bulletin Board (EBB)

Transportation Services Application (TSA)

Transportation Services Application RI (TSA-RI) 

Broker Management System (BMS)

Company Managed Contract Services (CMCS)
These applications are characterized as being at risk due to dependency upon aging 
application and operating technologies with limited support, unable to deliver changing 
regulatory requirements, and serve as an obstruction to aligning the RI program with the same 
capabilities as MA.  
The Gas Supply/ Retail Choice application functions were replaced in downstate New York by 
the Gas Transportation Information System (GTIS), started in 2011 and deployed in 2016. 
This proposal for strategic investment of $13.8M over 3 years will provide: 
o
Upgrade GTIS core application to current technology releases
o
Apply upgrades to support current operating systems and browsers
o
Upgrade hosting environment to increase system capacity
o
Migrate remaining regions to GTIS thereby leveraging GTIS capabilities,  reducing 
operational risks, and driving the retirement of the legacy application estate.            
Niagara Mohawk Power Corporation
d/b/a National Grid
Cases 20-E-0380 & 20-G-0381
