5
Business Case Analysis 
Business risks should EBB-Microstrategy application take an extended outage:
ESCOs unable to nominate volumes to Nationalgrid ;
Nationalgrid unable to confirm proper volumes, must rely on Pipeline EBB;
Nationalgrid unable to notify marketers through the application;
Pipeline penalties for inaccurate gas amounts can reach/ exceed $100 per dekatherm; 
Regulatory required communications impacted/ suspended; ESCOs could deny responsibility for 
penalties without official notification;
System operation in jeopardy during cold periods if unable to properly direct ESCOs and power gen;
ESCOs could seek damages from any penalties incurred on their part
Negative downstream impact to billing applications TSA, TSA-RI, BMS/CMCS
Potential for cost impacts: 
Pipeline penalties for 10,000 dTH @ $20/dTH x 60 days = $12M / year   
Regulatory fines of $1M/ Day in all regions  
An extended outage of TSA, TSA-RI, and/or BMS/CMCS applications would negatively impact 
Retail Choice program operations in effected regions:
Calculation of Marketer bill pools, storage, daily requirements, and imbalance reports
Reconciliation against the customer accounts
Support of 70+ ESCO’s and 144k Customers in NY, MA, and RI 
Potential for cost impacts:
Esco Billing of $30M (Annually, NiMO, MA, RI)
Potential to be out of compliance with tariff resulting in regulatory fines

d/b/a National Grid

6
Business Case Analysis 
The following processes are currently supported manually by NG resources due to capability  
limitations of legacy applications:    
1.
Gas Control Confirmation of Nominations – Gas Control manually confirms over 1,400 
nominations daily across all regions.  Automating this process in GTIS using an EDI data 
feed will save 2.5 FTE’s effort and result in reduced department costs.     

Financial Impact: Type 1: FTE Costs $500,000 Annually
2.
Manual processes to be automated in GTIS: 

Automating the manual calculation of UNY capacity release;

Upgrading the ESCO Aggregator relationship removes the need for manual 
aggregation data reducing risks associated with manual intervention and allows for 
access of required data in a usable format to other operating areas;

Incorporating an ICE calendar removes a manual workaround that does not provide a 
historical audit trail of the assigned holiday. Adding this calendar aligns the National 
Grid third party requirements calculation schedule with the Intercontinental Exchange 
(ICE) trading schedule;

Financial Impact: Type 2: FTE Costs $200K Annually.
Note: “Type 1” financial impact results in adjustment to department budget.

16
Legacy Application Interruptions  
The EBB application used to support daily gas 
scheduling by recording gas contracts, gas amounts, 
and confirmations is at risk due to its dependency on  
aging technology.  An outage in August 2019 
prevented internal and external users from accessing, 
entering, and viewing nominations putting NG at risk 
of fines and stopping business processes during the 
outage.   
Note:  A study in FY18 identified “Quorum” as a 
replacement for EBB functionality at a cost of $10M 
over 2 years for implementation.  The investment was 
funded in FY19 but stopped to re-evaluate options for  
addressing the complete requirement for Gas 
Operations and Retail Choice.

118 Reviews requirements and establishes a DevOps strategy for the project

EA
Functional
138 Creates the roadmap and regulations guiding IT designs and implementation within a business organization

Project Manager
PM
Functional
113 Plans, budgets, oversees, and documents all aspects of project
Works closely with upper management and technical leads ensuring scope of work is understood and managed
Risk mitigation; Escalation; Executive Communication on an as needed basis
Aligning resources to the project deliverables
Quality Engineering Systems
QES
Functional
87 Reviews requirements and establishes a Test strategy for the project
Creates Test plans, Test Scenarios, Test Scripts etc.
Designs and executes integration, conversion, and application testing
Identifies and diagnoses any work-in-progress issues
Works with business to design and oversee User Acceptance Test
Maintains records of product tests and defects and summarize corrective actions taken
Reviews and refines the Requirements Traceability Matrix

Assumptions
5823C-Arial & Robotic Line Inspections Innovative Capabilities
This investment will support the continued evaluation and development of new 
technologies in the Electric Transmission business supporting inspection,
maintenance, and efficient operations of physical transmission assets deployed in the 
field, including demonstration of aerial and terrestrial robotic line inspection, 
transformer and line dynamic rating, fault detection and location, and other emerging 
technologies. 
Scope:   
Networking to support technologies deployed to field;
Security and penetration testing solutions;
Application configuration & deployments;
Hosting services.
Delivery of investments in spread over FY23 - FY25 timeframe 
Duration is 36 months with yearly deployments of capabilities 
Assuming waterfall approach for executing each wave of implementation  
Assume vendor professional services leveraged for configuration
ADAM partners to be engaged 
Assume IT/ ADAM partner supported solution.  
Estimated 7/31/2020 by Doug McCarthy, Business Partners.  
ROM tolerance (-50/+200%). Subject to refinement as work progresses.

5877B - Business Issue Remediation Initiative
This Program will provide funding for IT investments required to improve Electric 
Substation Engineering critical business processes and resolve technology issues 
impeding business progress, to be delivered through a multi year Agile format:

Modernization Program;

value to utility customers.

implememtations of new or enhanced capabilities.

Assumptions
5877C-Engineering Application Rationalization
The engineering departments are dependent upon a portfolio of ~200 software titles, 
at various release levels, vendor support, and without any central management or 
governance, creating risk to these area's delivery capability.   This investment will 
include a study of this application portfolio, applying the rigor of Application 
Rationalization, and bring the software under IT support, change control, and 
management.  In Scope:
  Address issues associated with ~200 business supported applications supporting 
engineering organization    
  Determine applications in use and user base
  Create capability map of current application landscape/ Identify capability gaps 
  Evaluate opportunities to standardize / optimize / upgrade toolsets
  Execute
Estimate is preliminary as work will not start until FY22
Work will begin with a Feasibility & Analysis Study of the application suite
Delivery of investments in spread over FY22 - FY25 timeframe (Two major 
deployments planned)
Assuming waterfall approach for executing each wave of implementation  
Upgrade to hardware / hosting environments assumed 
Software / Middleware software license purchases assumed 
Majority of solutions are desktop deployments or SaaS

In SEIOP testimony p. 150, and Exhibit __ (SEIOP-4), p. 3 of 3, Staff recommends
downward CAPEX adjustments of $17.000M in FY22, $0 in FY23, and $0 in FY24.  In
Exhibit __ (SITP-2), p. 4 of 5, Staff recommends downward adjustments of $12.520M in
FY22, and $72.900M in FY23.  Please reconcile Staff’s proposed adjustments for the VOLT
Enablement program for FY22 and FY23.
b. Please show the calculation Staff used to arrive at the proposed RY downward adjustment of
$14.085 million for “”Staff Ind Projects removed” shown in Exhibit __ (SITP-2), p. 4 of 5.
i.
What individual projects make up the $14.085 million adjustment?
ii. What is the basis for the 33.8% adjustment shown in note 4?
c.
Please separately list each individual project and the corresponding adjustments that
comprise the $50,838,336 “Staff adj to remove specific projects” in Exhibit __ (SITP-2), p. 1
of 5, and “Staff Ind Projects removed” in Exhibit __ (SITP-2), p. 4 of 5.
d. In Exhibit__(SITP-2), p. 4 of 5, Staff shows an additional $11.819 million reduction to
VOLT Enablement as part of the Rate Year “Forecasting Adjustment.”  Please indicate
where this additional reduction is reflected in the Service Company Rents model.  If it is not
reflected in the model, please address and provide a reconciled Exhibit__(SITP-2).
Response: 
a.
Exhibit___(SITP-2) erroneously reflected downward adjustments to the VOLT Enablement
Program in the amount of $12.520M and $72.900M for FY 22 and FY 23, respectively.  The
Exhibit __ (ITP-1R)

Electric & Gas Rates 
NMPC-16 continued. 
- 2 -
Exhibit should have only reflected a downward adjustment in FY 22 in the amount of 
$17.000M.  Further, Exhibit___(SITP-2) contained additional errors related to the Grid 
Modernization Program.  For FY 22 and FY 23, the adjustments to the Grid Modernization 
Program should have reflected downward adjustments in the amount of $7.570M and 
$12.861M  for FY22 and FY23, respectively.  This did not impact the rest of the workpaper 
or exhibits.  Therefore, in the Rate Year the aggregate amount of our adjustments should 
have been $49.503M rather than $50.838M.  A corrected version of the exhibits and 
workpapers are attached to this response as Attachments 1 and 2, respectively. 
b. Staff did not adjust individual project lines within the VOLT Enablement Program, rather we
reduced the full Rate Year planned capital spending in FY22 by $12.520M, corrected in
response 1, above, to $17.000M.  We then converted the reduction in capital spending from
Fiscal Year to Rate Year and developed an adjustment factor of 33.8%, which we used to
adjust the capex spending in the Company’s Service Company Rents model.  The initial
adjustment factor of 33.8% was derived by dividing the $14.085M by the RY VOLT planned
spend of $41.700M.  It should be noted that the adjustment factor of 33.8% was incorrect and
should have been 30.6%, as shown in the Attachment 1 to this response.
c.
As stated in the response to question a, above, the $50.838M should have been $49.503M.
The individual projects include:
i.
CIS Project INVP# 5503B, FY22=$14.113M, FY23=$69.102M, which gets
translated to the Rate Year as $27.861M;
ii.
Grid Mod Projects INVP# 5471V and 5471M.  For INVP#5471V, the
adjustments are FY22=$0.763M, FY23=$0.764M, which gets translated to the
Rate Year as $0.764M.  For INVP# 5471M, the adjustments are FY22=$6.807M,
FY23=$12.098M, which translates to the Rate Year as $8.130M.  For a total
adjustment to Grid Mod for individual projects of $8.893M.
iii.
As stated in response b. above, the VOLT program spend on each project was
adjusted by a percentage in FY22 to reduce the FY22 budget by $17.000M, which
translates to the Rate Year as $12.750M (as corrected).
These corrections also impact the SITP recommended RY OPEX and RTB costs.  The 
original SITP Exhibit__(SITP-2) indicated a rate allowance in the Rate Year for incremental 
Service Company OPEX and RTB costs of approximately $66.671M.  Based on the 
corrections identified in this response, the SITP recommends a rate allowance in the Rate 
Year of $66.869M, which is shown in our revised workpapers, provided as Attachment 2 to 
this response. 
d. The Service Company Rents model should have included an additional adjustment to the
VOLT Program to reflect Staff’s forecasting adjustment in the amount of $12.390M.  The
